queries.hook: I'm anxious about how things will turn out. Inside, my mind won't settle, and I don't know how to carry it.
queries.diagnose: The mind suffers when it clings to results it cannot control; gripping the outcome turns honest effort into anxiety.
queries.steady: Your part is the effort, not the outcome; work done well is already complete, whatever result comes.
queries.act: Do your work fully and well, then let the result go; your part is the effort, not the fruit.
queries.story: A story of a seeker whose mind will not settle, facing holding on to how it turns out.

plan_v3.first_line: You feel your mind reel with restlessness, yet you still strive to find your footing.

hook.speaker: Arjuna
hook.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
hook.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचयोऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन । एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥
hook.line: This calm you describe, Krishna, I can't see it lasting. My mind is too restless.
hook.translation: Arjuna said: This yoga of evenness that you have taught, Madhusudana, I do not see how it can last, because of restlessness.
hook.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

alternates.speaker: Arjuna
alternates.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
alternates.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचअयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः । अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥
alternates.line: What happens to someone who believes, tries, slips, and doesn't make it to the end?
alternates.translation: Arjuna said: One who has faith but does not strive enough, whose mind falls away from yoga before reaching perfection, what end does he come to, Krishna?
alternates.why: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

prasang.title: What becomes of one who falls from yoga
prasang.summary: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.
prasang.lesson: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.
